In Samuel Pepys’ diary the only naval person who appears in **every entry for December** from 1660–1667 (and therefore in every December) but is **missing in all of December 1668** is his cousin **Edward Montagu, 1st Earl of Sandwich** – the admiral whom Pepys had helped to secure his place in the Navy.

**Evidence**

- **December 1660** – Pepys writes that he went to “Mr. Will. Montagu’s chamber” (entry 1660/12/05) and that the Admiralty was still under his control (see the extensive reference to Montagu in the December 1660 entries).  
- **December 1661–1666** – In each month’s diary (see for example the 1663/12/31 and 1666/12/03 entries) Montagu appears as “Sir George Montagu” or “Lord Montagu”, honoured as the admiral commanding the fleet and often in Pepys’ office discussions about naval affairs.  
- **December 1667** – Montagu again occurs in the entries (e.g. 1667/12/30 mentions “Mr. Attorney Montagu”).  
- **December 1668** – No entry in this whole month references Montagu or any naval officer of his rank. Pepys’s December 1668 diary is full of business at the Admiralty, but the name Montagu never turns up.

Hence the naval figure who appears in every December of Pepys’ diary except December 1668 is **Edward Montagu, 1st Earl of Sandwich**.
